minutes.headline: Superintendent outlined FY25 staffing cuts across all categories to meet a 2.5% target and a possible 10% health insurance rise.
minutes.summary: The committee heard the superintendent's one-page summary of possible staffing reductions by category, driven by the loss of Esser money and a budgeted health insurance increase. They also discussed the 2024-25 calendar (December closure and January return), accepted a small donation, and heard a member recuse himself from contract negotiations on ethics advice. The meeting ended with a vote to go into executive session on collective bargaining and adjourn.

what_happened.line: The superintendent presented a one-page summary of possible FY25 staffing reductions by category, tied to the loss of Esser grant money.
The FY25 target is a 2.5% increase, and the budget carries a possible 10% rise in health insurance; the actual rate arrives in late February.
A member asked whether the cuts close the gap; the superintendent said the gap is closer to the larger of the figures discussed.
A Box Tops for Education donation to the Turkey Hill gift account was put to a vote; the outcome was not audible in the captions.
Budget approval is targeted for March with a public hearing the night before; the committee leaned toward a December Monday off in the 2024-25 calendar.

why_it_matters: The staffing cuts and the health insurance assumption both feed the school budget residents will vote on, so a different insurance rate in February could change how large the cuts need to be.
Esser money was federal one-time funding, so positions it paid for either end or move onto the town-funded budget, which bears on the school line of the tax bill.
watch_next: The actual health insurance rate, expected in late February.
The March budget approval and the public hearing the night before, with dates still to be confirmed with the finance committee.
